acceptance: `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` succeed on a clean checkout with no network access, and go.mod gains no `require` block — standard library only, no vendor directory, language level `go 1.23` with no stdlib or language feature newer than 1.23.

`go test ./...` passes, and its cases cover at minimum: all five `event` values including `grafted`; an event with no `role`; an event with no `usage` object; `usage.known == false`; `usage.known == true` with `cost_usd` present; `usage.known == true` with `cost_usd` absent; a malformed non-JSON line; a line missing a required field; an empty input; and a line longer than bufio.Scanner's default 64KiB token limit (design risk 4).
Given a fixture log, the tool prints one block containing a per-`node_id` section and a per-`role` section, each carrying counts of `dispatched`, `complete`, `failed`, and `merged`.

For a fixture whose known-and-priced events are `0.12` and `0.34`, the printed total is `0.4600`, and the printed unpriced count is exactly the number of events in that fixture that are not known-and-priced.

Only events with `usage.known == true` AND `cost_usd` present contribute to the total: adding an event with `usage.known == false`, or with no `usage` object, to a fixture leaves the printed total figure byte-identical. All three unpriced shapes (no `usage`; `known == false`; `known == true` without `cost_usd`) are counted as unpriced, never summed as 0.

Determinism: running the tool twice on the same input produces byte-identical stdout. Rows appear in a documented sort order — `node_id` and `role` ascending by byte order — never Go map order, and cost is accumulated in that same sorted order so float64 addition is reproducible run to run.

The block reports lines read, events counted, and lines skipped, and states which of the reported numbers a reader can add up to the reported line count. `grafted` events and unrecognized `event` values are reported in that accounting line rather than discarded, so schema drift shows up as a nonzero count instead of a wrong summary.

Exit status is 0 whenever a summary was printed, and non-zero with a message on stderr when the input could not be read at all. A skipped line alone does not fail the run; skipped lines are tallied and noted on stderr, not fatal and not silent.

The tool reads one input only (no globbing, no directory walking, no multiple files), writes nothing but stdout/stderr and its exit code, makes no network access, and never mutates the run log. Test fixtures are self-contained — inline strings or `testdata/` — never a real effort's log from elsewhere on the machine.
Stays inside the declared surface: `*.go` at the repo root, `internal/`, and `testdata/`. README.md and docs/ belong to the docs node and are not touched here.
intent: Implement the standalone runlog-stats CLI and its own tests: read one run-log.jsonl (positional path, or stdin when the path is absent or '-'), parse the field subset the tool consumes (node_id, event, role, usage.known, usage.cost_usd), count dispatched/complete/failed/merged per node_id and per role, sum cost over events that are known-and-priced only, report every unpriced event as its own count that is never added into the total, render one deterministic plain-text block to stdout, and set the exit code. Standard library only, read-only and offline, with the parse/count/render seam reachable from tests over an io.Reader and an io.Writer so tests need not exec a binary. Whether that seam is a second file in package main or a small internal/ package is this node's call (design decision 9); a cmd/ layout is unnecessary for a single binary.
